Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 – Summary (The Real Alternative)

Core principles and funding
- Principles: Freedom, fairness, trust, with a “green thread” through all policies and strong internationalism.
- Costings: Switch about £5bn/year from low-priority spend (abolish many DTI subsidies, scrap ID cards, redirect the Child Trust Fund). Introduce a 50% tax only on income over £100,000 to fund three pledges: abolish student tuition/top-up fees, free personal care for elderly/disabled, and lower local taxes.
- Fairer local taxation: Scrap Council Tax; introduce Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450; 8 in 10 pensioners pay less).

Health
- Free personal care for elderly/disabled (as in Scotland).
- Faster diagnosis via public or private capacity; more scans out of hours; publish test waiting times.
- End charges for eye/dental check-ups; widen prescription exemptions.
- More frontline staff; scrap central targets; empower local democratic control.
- Reform NHS dentistry; expand palliative and mental health rights; strong prevention (nutrition standards, restrict junk ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places).

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore maintenance grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund money to hire 21,000 teachers; cut infant classes to avg 20 and junior to 25; expand wraparound care and Children’s Centres.
- Qualified teachers for core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing; stronger discipline and SEN support.
- Integrated academic/vocational diplomas; fund FE fairly; protect free school transport distances.

Crime, justice and liberties
- Fund 10,000 extra police by scrapping ID cards; complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy.
- Tough community sentences for non-violent offenders; tackle binge drinking; focus on drug trafficking and crime-linked use.
- Make prisons educate and skill for work; UK Border Force for security.
- Repeal flawed control-order regime; admit intercept evidence; Single Equality Act; hate-crime units.
- Fair asylum system via independent agency; allow asylum seekers to work.

Economy and business
- Fiscal stability; NAO to audit Budget; ONS independence; curb irresponsible lending.
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax; raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.
- Cut red tape (sunset clauses; single inspections); small business rate relief; abolish DTI and reinvest savings; duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.

Pensions and welfare
- Citizen’s Pension from 75, linked to earnings: +£100+/month for singles; removes means tests for ~1m.
- Local Income Tax benefits pensioners; maternity income guarantee (£170/week for 6 months for first child).
- Reform New Deal; scrap CSA and move to Inland Revenue; winter fuel payment to severely disabled; stronger pension loss compensation; cut fraud and error.

Local communities and housing
- Free councils from Whitehall controls; merge inspectorates; protect post offices and universal service.
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; incentivise brownfield reuse; manage second homes; support arts, heritage and grassroots sport.

Transport
- Fix rail with fewer, longer franchises; prioritise safety and key upgrades.
- Reward low-emission cars via VED reform; expand congestion charging and, long term, replace fuel duty/VED with national road pricing.
- Free off-peak bus travel for pensioners/disabled; shift funds from new roads to public transport; expand rail freight; per-aircraft aviation charges; oppose SE airport expansion.

Rural affairs
- Fair prices for farmers (duty to trade fairly; Food Trade Inspector); faster CAP reform; Marine Act; stronger animal welfare; precaution on GM, promote organic.

Europe, defence, and international development
- Opposed Iraq war; aim to withdraw UK troops with UN mandate expiry; rebuild via inclusive politics and services.
- Support EU Constitution (referendum), euro entry when conditions met; UN/EU reform; rights-based foreign policy.
- Maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; stricter arms export oversight.
- Aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; fairer trade (end dumping); green development focus.

Better government
- Curb PM powers; War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger Select Committees.
- Fewer departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; STV for elections (including Commons); predominantly elected second chamber; votes at the age people can marry/leave school/start work; independent BBC regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; consolidate environment/transport/energy in one department.
- Climate targets: at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; carbon-focused taxes; no new nuclear; “contraction and convergence” long-term goal.
